memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At once the Lord said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, "Come out to the tent of meeting, all three of you." So the three of them went out. Then the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud; he stood at the entrance to the tent and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When the two of them stepped forward, — Num 12:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God responds "at once." He does not let the poison of jealousy fester or spread through the camp. When His servant is being wrongly attacked, He steps in quickly and calls all three siblings before Him. There is something reassuring in this promptness — God is not slow or indifferent to injustice, even when we cannot see Him acting yet.

The Lord comes down in the pillar of cloud, His visible presence, and stands at the tent's entrance. This is a courtroom scene, and God Himself is the judge. Miriam and Aaron thought they were having a private conversation about their brother. Now they find themselves standing before the living God to answer for it.

There is a healthy weight to this moment. We can grow so casual about our words and attitudes, forgetting that we live every day in the presence of God. One day every one of us will stand before Him and give an account. That is not meant to crush us but to sober us — to make us take our words, our motives, and our treatment of others seriously.

Yet for those who belong to Christ, this coming judgment holds no terror. The One who will judge is also the One who died to save. We can walk into God's presence not as trembling defendants but as forgiven children, because Jesus has already answered for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How would your words change if you remembered you live in God's presence?
2. Why does God act quickly to protect His servant here?
3. How does knowing Christ has answered for you change how you face God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a just God who does not ignore wrong. Help me to live mindful of Your presence, and to rest in Christ who answered for me before You. Amen.
